title: Mach9 raises $34M Series A after pivot to AI-assisted CAD software
description: The company, founded in 2021 as Mach9 Robotics, says nearly 100 private-beta customers have used its AI CAD tool on more than 2,500 projects. First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners co-led the round.
body: Mach9 has raised a $34 million Series A round co-led by First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners, the company announced, according to TechCrunch. Prudence, an early-stage New York firm that invests in AI software use cases for construction and real estate, and Quiet Capital, a venture firm already on Mach9's cap table, also participated. The funding follows a change of direction. When Alex Baikovitz co-founded the company as Mach9 Robotics in 2021, the goal was to give civil engineers a better, faster and cheaper way to carry out visual inspections. The company later dropped "Robotics" from its name and pivoted to developing AI-powered computer-aided design software instead. According to TechCrunch, that bet has produced nearly 100 customers for the private beta of Mach9's software, and those users have applied it to more than 2,500 projects to date. Baikovitz described CAD as one of the slowest and most labor-intensive parts of the civil engineering pipeline. He told TechCrunch that delivering a project can take months, and that manual work in legacy incumbent software built by companies such as Autodesk and Bentley Systems runs at roughly a week per mile. Mach9 says its software automates much of that work, making the process 10 times faster and sharply reducing costs. On the technical side, Baikovitz said Mach9 developed and trained its own in-house AI models to reach the centimeter-level accuracy that construction and infrastructure work requires. He described the development effort since 2024 as centered on building models that can turn imagery, or combined image and laser-scan datasets, into survey-grade geometry, tracing features such as curbs and pavement striping to the precision and format customers expect. In use, the system takes survey data and produces a first draft of a plan, which engineers then refine. Baikovitz said the software gives users tools to draw, remove and adjust vertices and to assess the quality of the AI-generated model, so that licensed professionals can put their names behind the deliverable. He pointed to the liability involved in the industry and the need for licensed professionals who understand what they are reviewing. As for the new funding, Baikovitz said Mach9 will divide it between improving the product, hiring industry experts and scaling "all parts of our organization to keep up with where the market is taking us."

title: Recursive Releases Flint, a Free Laptop Coding Model It Says AI Largely Built
description: The startup says its Eureka Machine assisted nearly every stage of Flint's development, yielding a 40 billion parameter model that runs offline and is free to download under an open source license.
body: Recursive, an AI startup founded last year, released its first model on Wednesday. The company, which says it is working toward AI that can improve itself, calls the model Flint: a free coding model that runs on a laptop and was built largely with AI assistance, according to TechCrunch. Recursive credits its automated research system, the Eureka Machine, with helping at nearly every stage of Flint's development. The company says that assistance let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. The Eureka Machine generates ideas, runs experiments, and uses the outcomes to choose what to attempt next. As TechCrunch describes it, what Recursive has deployed so far is narrower than its long-term ambition: an AI research assistant supervised by people, which produced a model small enough to run on a laptop. Recursive did not say how much researcher time the Eureka Machine saved, and it is not the only organization turning to AI to support research work. Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it engages only a fraction of its capacity for any given task. It has 40 billion parameters in total but uses 2.5 billion of them at a time. The model is free to download on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits free use and modification. Because Flint runs on the user's own computer instead of a company's cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that cloud AI services charge based on how much text a model processes, according to TechCrunch. In Recursive's own testing, Flint generated about 131 tokens, or chunks of text, per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple's M4 Pro chip. The company says that is roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that comparable models reached on the same machine, including Google's Gemma 4 and Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Recursive also says Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters on SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs. Both results come from the company rather than independent evaluation. Recursive acknowledged that Flint requires more guidance than the large paid coding assistants and suggested that users break large tasks into smaller steps. The release is the first model from a company whose stated goal is self-improving AI, and the Eureka Machine's role in building Flint offers an early, limited example of that approach in practice.

title: Canva Launches Canva Craft, Its First In-House Image Generation Model
description: The design platform says the model, built by its research team with contributions from Leonardo.ai researchers, is available now through the Dream Lab tab, with API access planned.
body: Canva has introduced Canva Craft, its first image generation model, TechCrunch reported. The design platform built the model within its own research team and intends it to compete with comparable image generators from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance and Meta, according to the report. TechCrunch describes the generation process as two distinct phases. In the first, Canva Craft reads the user's prompt and drafts a composition plan covering how elements are positioned relative to one another, their comparative sizes, the visual hierarchy of the image and the information needed to render any text. The second phase turns that plan into the finished image, which can reach up to 2K resolution and be produced in as many as 30 aspect ratios for use across different platforms. According to the report, users would also be able to make targeted edits to an image without altering the rest of it. Images produced with Canva Craft could then be turned into layered designs through Canva Magic, the company's tool for converting an image into an editable design. Canva Craft is available on Canva's platform to all users, who can open it from the Dream Lab tab, TechCrunch reported. The company also plans to offer the model through the Canva API, a future step rather than a current feature. The release builds on Canva's 2024 acquisition of Leonardo.ai, a media generation platform. Canva said researchers from Leonardo took part in developing the new model, according to TechCrunch. The report also noted that the company was on track for $4 billion in revenue last year.

title: Nirva Raises $25M as It Prepares a Voice-Filtering AI Pendant
description: The startup, founded by two former Meta Reality Labs employees and a fashion entrepreneur, announced a $25 million pre-Series A round. Its $249 pendant is set to take orders in November.
body: Nirva, a startup building a jewelry-like wearable pendant, announced a $25 million pre-Series A round, TechCrunch reported. The new funding adds to $8 million the company raised earlier in the year from investors including Lightspeed and South Park Commons, bringing its total raise to $33 million. The company was founded in 2025 by Wei Lyu and Jason Chen, both former Meta Reality Labs employees, along with Hanying Hu, who founded a fashion and jewelry brand. Lyu is Nirva's CEO. Nirva's first device is a pendant that can also be worn as a bracelet. It weighs about eight grams, which the company presents as making it easy to wear throughout the day, and its battery is rated to last up to three days on a single charge. The device is priced at $249 and will be offered in silver, brushed silver, black and gold. According to TechCrunch's reporting, the company's approach to the privacy question that hangs over ambient devices rests on how the product is set up and what it does with captured audio. During onboarding, users are asked to record snippets of their voice, and Nirva builds its model from those samples. In use, the device filters out conversations or data captured from other people around it, according to the company. Nirva also says that by default it does not keep audio data or transcripts once conversations have been processed. Before discarding the audio, the company says, it tracks tone, pitch, volume and speed, attributes it describes as useful for deriving emotion-related understandings that are then surfaced in the app. The companion app parses the wearer's speech and produces insights the company infers are related to the user's personality. TechCrunch reported that these include patterns, the people who tend to be around the user, the places they have been and other daily notes. Privacy is a central concern for ambient devices, since people may not want to be recorded all the time. Nirva's stated design choices, from voice enrollment to filtering and default deletion, are the company's account of how the product addresses that concern. Nirva positions itself as a personal insights company rather than a productivity startup. In a call with TechCrunch, Lyu said the company wanted to build a wearable that blends in with fashion while also providing value to users. Nirva says orders are expected to open in November. Its stated goal is to dispatch the first units to early users before year-end.

title: Commerce Letters of Intent Cover Up to $389 Million in Energy Semiconductor R&D
description: Four companies are named for potential CHIPS Act awards covering fusion power electronics, gallium nitride devices and ultra-high-purity quartz, with Helion's share the largest at up to $175 million.
body: The Department of Commerce has signed letters of intent with four companies that would provide up to $389 million in federal research and development awards under the CHIPS and Science Act, the National Institute of Standards and Technology announced. The proposed funding is aimed at semiconductors and materials involved in controlling, converting and delivering power. The four recipients named are Helion, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Vertical Semiconductor and Sibelco. Each figure is a maximum described in a letter of intent, not a completed award. Helion's share would be the largest, at up to $175 million, for developing and scaling domestic work on high-voltage power semiconductors and advanced energy power modules built for pulsed-power use with high peak currents in fusion generation. NIST said the devices would manage power for the magnets that drive Helion's fusion generators, including controlling and harvesting energy from them. Commonwealth Fusion Systems would receive up to $85 million for R&D on several electronics categories: semiconductors for radio-frequency plasma heating, power electronics, embedded electronics used in fusion diagnostics, and components designed to withstand radiation. Vertical Semiconductor is named for up to $73 million to advance its vertical gallium nitride power semiconductors, which the agency said could make power delivery for advanced computing more efficient and compact. The work would also include demonstrating the technology for what the announcement called the world's first 2.5 MW super intelligence data center rack. Sibelco would receive up to $56 million for R&D on purification and finishing methods for ultra-high-purity quartz. The material is used in crucibles for crystal growth, in processing glassware and in other hardware across the semiconductor value chain, and NIST said the work is meant to supply next-generation ultra-high-purity quartz to support the domestic supply chain. According to the agency, better power converter performance can bring higher power efficiency, improved grid stability and lower thermal losses. TechCrunch described the proposed Helion support as a three-year CHIPS Act award. It described the Biden-era law as intended to strengthen U.S. research, development and manufacturing of semiconductor modules. Helion announced the funding on Thursday, the publication reported. Helion's existing power devices lose roughly 5% to 10% of the electricity passing through them, according to TechCrunch. The report said the funding would help the company build automated capacity for semiconductor modules, packaging and testing to supply the fusion machine now under construction. TechCrunch quoted Helion's Kirtley saying no U.S. manufacturers currently perform that work. The report also said more than $100 million would be set aside for semiconductor and advanced packaging R&D in Washington State, while about $80 million would support R&D in Vermont on advanced semiconductor tooling, design and process development with GlobalFoundries. Separately, TechCrunch reported that GlobalFoundries has received more than $80 million from the federal government to advance manufacturing of gallium-nitride semiconductors, a type widely used in power electronics. Helion is working to finish its first power plant, Orion, in time for a 2028 deadline to supply Microsoft with electricity from the grid, TechCrunch reported. Kirtley acknowledged that the R&D funded by the award would not reach Orion in time for its launch, because federal contracts can take months to negotiate, according to the publication. He said the work could improve efficiency at later Helion plants and their ability to compete in electricity markets. TechCrunch also reported that Helion announced a new $50 million private investment alongside the federal funding but did not identify the investor. The company has raised more than $3.2 billion in total, making it the second-best-funded fusion startup, the publication reported. Helion says its approach, known as direct energy conversion, will help future reactors generate more power than they consume, a threshold any fusion plant must meet to be commercially viable, according to TechCrunch. Bill Frauenhofer, who leads semiconductor investment and innovation at Commerce, said in a press release that the award would help convert and deliver power to critical applications in defense, grid transmission and advanced energy generation, TechCrunch reported. Despite possible defense contracts, Kirtley said Helion remains focused on putting power on the grid, telling the publication that domestic energy supply, national security through energy dominance and energy security are its main focus.

title: Meta Plans New Non-Voting Share Class to Help Fund AI Push
description: The company confirmed on its third-quarter earnings call that it intends to distribute a new class of non-voting stock to existing shareholders, with trading expected to begin in 2027.
body: Meta plans to create a new class of non-voting stock that could help finance its artificial intelligence buildout, a plan the company confirmed during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday. The move was first reported by Semafor, according to TechCrunch, which said the shares would carry no vote on company decisions. Finance chief Susan Li said existing shareholders would receive the planned non-voting capital stock through a stock dividend, TechCrunch reported. The Verge identified potential acquisitions and employee compensation as additional uses for the shares. The share plan arrives alongside quarterly results that TechCrunch described as strong and ahead of Wall Street expectations. Costs and expenses rose as well, by 68% year over year, according to the same report. Meta's Reality Labs division, which houses its AR glasses, VR headsets and VR software, continues to lose money, though TechCrunch reported the losses are smaller than they once were. The company said in its earnings report that it expects the division's losses to shrink from 2025 levels to between $18 billion and $19 billion. Meta has expanded its AI lineup over the past year. TechCrunch reported that the company released several models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year, and in recent weeks added Muse Wonder and Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model whose underlying parameters are publicly available for outsiders to use and build on. Zuckerberg also reported uptake of Meta's personal agents during the call. According to TechCrunch, he said more than 10 million people had set them up in the U.S. and Canada over a month and a half. The Verge reported that trading in the new share class would begin in 2027. The share distribution remains a company plan, as described by Li in the account from TechCrunch.

title: Tesla Says It Will Sell Cybercab to Customers by End of Year, TechCrunch Reports
description: The announcement comes as federal regulators examine whether the vehicle meets safety standards, according to TechCrunch. Tesla's CEO framed the Cybercab as transport-as-a-service rather than a car for owners.
body: Tesla said Wednesday that it will begin selling its Cybercab to customers before the end of the year, TechCrunch reported, even as federal regulators are investigating whether the vehicle complies with vehicle safety standards. According to TechCrunch, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the federal auto safety regulator, announced last month that it had opened an investigation into the Cybercab. TechCrunch placed that announcement just hours after the vehicles began operating on public streets in Austin. TechCrunch reported that current regulations do not accommodate vehicles without manual controls. The Department of Transportation has recently proposed removing those requirements for vehicles designed to be driven autonomously, according to the report. On a Wednesday call, Tesla CEO Elon Musk described the Cybercab as primarily a transport-as-a-service offering, distinct from models such as the 3, the Y and the Roadster that he cast as cars customers would want to own, TechCrunch reported. TechCrunch reported that Musk has discussed building a large fleet of low-cost robotaxis for years, but that until recently those plans focused on converting privately owned Tesla vehicles into self-driving taxis through a software update. The timing of the sales commitment places it alongside the unresolved regulatory question.

title: Japan's MMX probe heads for Phobos on sample-return voyage
description: The $578 million mission is in stable condition after launch, with a rover drop and up to two Phobos landings planned before a 2030 departure from Mars and a 2031 capsule landing in South Australia.
body: Japan has sent a $578 million spacecraft toward Mars's largest moon, Phobos, on a five-year round trip intended to bring samples back to Earth, Ars Technica reported. The outlet described the project as an international endeavor that could shed light on how the Solar System formed. Once it separated from the H3 rocket, the MMX probe got in touch with ground controllers and deployed its solar arrays, Ars Technica reported. Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, the mission's project manager at JAXA, described the spacecraft as being in a "very stable condition." Under the current plan, the Phobos survey phase would reach its peak in late 2028 or early 2029, when the MMX mothership releases a small rover to descend to the moon's surface. The mission's most demanding step is scheduled for later in 2029, when the main craft would try as many as two landings on Phobos. Because Phobos's gravity is weak and irregular, a lander risks toppling or rebounding into space. Ars Technica reported that the probe's landing gear is built to take in the force of each touchdown to lower that risk. After lifting off Phobos, MMX would jettison the landing gear and, in 2030, burn its engines to set a course for Earth. The following year, the spacecraft would steer a sample capsule down to a remote site in South Australia, according to Ars Technica.

title: Rays Take AL Pennant, Set Up First-Title World Series Against Brewers
description: Tampa Bay closed out Cleveland in Game 6 of the ALCS and will meet Milwaukee in a Fall Classic where neither club has won a championship. Game 1 is Friday in Milwaukee.
body: The Tampa Bay Rays secured the American League pennant by defeating the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the ALCS on Monday night, NPR reported. It is the franchise's third pennant across 29 major league seasons. Díaz and Junior Caminero both connected for two-run home runs in the clincher. Freddy Peralta worked 5 1/3 innings for Tampa Bay. Caminero had 42 home runs during the regular season but required 33 at-bats before hitting his first of October, according to NPR. The Rays now meet the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers. According to NPR, it is the first World Series in which both participants are chasing their first title since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies defeated the Kansas City Royals. Game 1 is set for Friday night in Milwaukee. Tampa Bay's path to the ALCS included a Division Series sweep of the New York Yankees. Once in the championship series, the Rays trailed the Guardians 1-0 and then 2-1 before winning three consecutive games to take the pennant.

title: Report: Anthropic and Nscale in Talks on Another $45B Compute Deal
description: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, says the two companies could announce a second $45 billion compute agreement about a month after their first, though talks are ongoing and terms may change.
body: Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale may be preparing a second $45 billion compute agreement, roughly a month after announcing a deal of the same size, TechCrunch reported, citing Bloomberg. According to the report, people familiar with the matter said the two companies were close to announcing the new deal. Those sources also cautioned that negotiations were still in progress and that the terms could change. TechCrunch said it had contacted Nscale and Anthropic for further information. If completed, the reported agreement would add to a series of large compute deals Anthropic has reached over the past year, the outlet said.

title: European Commission names 13 winners of 2026 New European Bauhaus Prizes
description: The laureates come from several EU countries, Ukraine, North Macedonia, Japan and Brazil, according to the Commission's announcement.
body: The European Commission has awarded the 2026 New European Bauhaus Prizes to 13 laureates, it said in a press release dated 16 October 2026. The winners come from several EU countries as well as Ukraine and North Macedonia, the Commission said. Japan and Brazil won the international competition of the awards, according to the same announcement.

title: Separate updates: RAISE launch and Tripartite Social Summit
description: Separate official notices: the European Commission launched RAISE in Europe; the Council reported a Tripartite Social Summit meeting in Brussels.
source_label: European Commission · Council of the European Union
body: The European Commission states that it launched the RAISE pledging initiative in Europe. According to the Council of the European Union, EU leaders and social partners met at the Tripartite Social Summit in Brussels. Editorial scope: Institutional notices are adapted and summarized as separate updates; this briefing does not claim a shared project or assess demonstrated outcomes.

title: Agency briefing: aid talks, household finances and science
description: Public-agency updates from October 8–9 cover development talks in Dublin, U.S. household finance data and science policy. Read the original sources.
body: In remarks dated October 9 in Dublin, European Commission Commissioner Hadja Lahbib described discussions on development held the previous evening. Her remarks linked humanitarian assistance with development work and referred to talks involving key stakeholders. This item summarizes that part of the announcement; it does not report a new funding commitment. The Federal Reserve Board announced the release of its 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances on October 9. The survey covers the financial circumstances of American families. The release links to data and a summary report comparing survey periods; readers can consult those materials for the findings. This short briefing does not summarize the survey results. In an October 8 announcement, NIST described its support for a White House science initiative. The agency connected its work on measurement and standards with scientific research and industrial applications. This brief attributes that position to NIST; it does not assess the initiative’s effectiveness or treat the agency’s promotional language as an established outcome.
